item.title: 隨身AI都是坑？軟體沒做完，客服沒招到？隱私給AI，我得到的是……｜大狸子切切裡
item.itunes:title: 隨身AI都是坑？軟體沒做完，客服沒招到？隱私給AI，我得到的是……｜大狸子切切裡
item.itunes:author: 大狸子切切裡 Cherry OFFICIAL CHANNEL
item.itunes:summary:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AJrJ96nR-BM

值得閱讀的理由

  • 開箱評測市面上三款熱門的隨身 AI 設備，直擊宣傳與實際體驗落差巨大的「踩坑」實況。
  • 深入剖析隨身 AI 設備在軟體成熟度、隱私政策、售後客服及硬體品質上的各種真實問題。
  • 反思當我們將日常記憶與情緒解釋權交給 AI 設備時，可能帶來的心理影響與隱憂。

摘要

在這部影片中，創作者實際買了三款宣傳得很吸引人的隨身 AI 設備來進行開箱與深度體驗，總結出「踩坑率高達三分之二」的實際心得。影片透過實測展示了這些產品在行銷與現實之間的落差。

第一款設備：Simpai

這款設備售價較高（影片提及價格區間如 1999 等），但體驗卻狀況百出。購買時發現連店鋪客服都找不到，軟體下載甚至需要透過 TestFlight，App Store 也搜尋不到，隱私政策與軟體許可協議缺乏中文版本，顯然並非針對中國大陸市場正規販售。透過 AI 查詢背景發現其為香港年輕團隊，群眾募資金額不高 [[02:15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AJrJ96nR-BM&t=135)]。實際使用 App 的時間軸與日記海報功能更像一本「答案之書」，生成的標題與內容十分荒誕、充滿雜音或隨機生成，甚至每張卡片結尾都會固定加上類似的情感對白。設備本身續航力差、夜間待機耗電嚴重、外殼氧化，且相機拍到的東西只轉換成文字不保留圖片，缺乏實質證據 [[04:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AJrJ96nR-BM&t=262)]。整體而言找不到優點，售後幾近為零。

第二款設備：Lucky（或類似發音的設備）

這款設備採用黑色樸素機身與磁吸充電器。與前一款不同，它使用起來「稍微有一點 AI 的感覺」 [[05:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AJrJ96nR-BM&t=335)]。它會每隔幾分鐘自動錄製短影片或記錄日常，雖然生成的卡通化圖片經常有手指或品種分不清的「幻覺」，但作為日常記憶碎片還算合適。最有趣的是它會主動發出關心或調侃的語音提醒（例如提醒餵貓、關心生物鐘等），甚至能通過觸控板長按進行對話、搜索記憶與識別場景。不過，長期佩戴也帶來了隱私疑慮，且每天生活重複時會顯得有些機械與沉重 [[08:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AJrJ96nR-BM&t=523)]。整體而言，這是三款中較有互動感的一款。

第三款設備：類似鵝卵石或吊墜造型的設備（Nana / N 系列）

外觀設計最像飾品，配有精美的小鍊子與鵝卵石充電底座，並藏有光體感應器可隔著衣服測量心跳與呼吸 [[09:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AJrJ96nR-BM&t=564)]。其核心能力是記錄心情、說話字數、實時語速及心律，幫助用戶收集快樂的卡片，並會自動記錄用戶去過的地方、看過的電影（例如古希臘神話與奧德修斯） [[10:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AJrJ96nR-BM&t=617)]。然而現實體驗同樣骨感，App 經常反覆詢問「有沒有變化」，且宣稱關注隱私的同時卻無法查看錄音原文 [[10:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AJrJ96nR-BM&t=657)]，客服回應緩慢。

創作者的深層省思

在花費了四千多元台幣／人民幣體驗這些隨身 AI 設備後，創作者提出了更深層的思考：當我們過度依賴 AI 記錄生活、甚至讓 AI 幫忙定義和解釋我們的情緒與記憶時，是否會不知不覺中把個人記憶與情緒的控制權逐漸移交給了 AI？這值得所有使用者深思。

=============

-------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------

item.title: iPhone Duo上手體驗！那個蘋果回來了，但沒有改變一切｜大狸子切切裡
item.itunes:title: iPhone Duo上手體驗！那個蘋果回來了，但沒有改變一切｜大狸子切切裡
item.itunes:author: 大狸子切切裡 Cherry OFFICIAL CHANNEL
item.itunes:summary:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pZjpBAh6S30

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入了解蘋果首款折疊機 iPhone Duo的實際手感、特殊開合機構與抗眩光螢幕的真實體驗。
  • 解析獨特的解鎖方式、按鍵配置與外觀設計邏輯，帶你看清蘋果在硬體與Liquid Glass介面上的深層佈局。
  • 客觀剖析大螢幕折疊機面臨的生態相容性痛點，揭示主流應用程式在適配過程中的妥協與挑戰。

摘要

極致工藝與初次上手的陌生感

作者指出，iPhone Duo作為蘋果多年來最為大膽的產品，在發售初期引發了極高的市場搶購熱潮。然而，當真正拿到手機時，除了折疊螢幕帶來的新鮮感，迎面而來的還有操作上的陌生感。其音量鍵位置偏高，機身保留了相機控制按鈕，但在喚醒與解鎖邏輯上需要重新適應。經過作者測試，需要透過特定順序的滑動與按壓組合才能達到最快解鎖，儘管這些細節有望在日後的軟體更新中逐步改善。

在展開手感方面，作者給予了極高評價。iPhone Duo擁有滑順且能單手輕鬆展開的機構設計，在完全打開時伴隨清脆的鎖定卡嗒聲，帶來療癒的感官回饋。手機內建的霧面抗眩光螢幕在降低折痕與抗反光效果上表現出色，雖然稍微犧牲了對比度與銳利度，但其紙質般的質感在閱讀長文本、瀏覽漫畫或日常多種光源環境下，皆展現出極致的高級感。

軟硬整合的設計哲學與視聽表現

作者分析，蘋果過去推廣的Liquid Glass設計語言，在 iPhone Duo 的霧面螢幕上找到了完美的歸宿。無論是視覺效果還是闔上手機時如關閉筆記本般的動畫，都體現了科技與人文的融合。針對備受關注的螢幕下前方相機，作者直言雖然仍能看出材質差異而並非完全隱形，但相較於傳統挖孔螢幕，視覺干擾已大幅降低。此外，該機在支援杜比視界（Dolby Vision）與外放揚聲器音質上的表現皆屬於業界頂尖水準。

軟體適配的現況、挑戰與未來展望

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入了解蘋果首款折疊機 iPhone Duo的實際手感、特殊開合機構與抗眩光螢幕的真實體驗。
  • 解析獨特的解鎖方式、按鍵配置與外觀設計邏輯，帶你看清蘋果在硬體與Liquid Glass介面上的深層佈局。
  • 客觀剖析大螢幕折疊機面臨的生態相容性痛點，揭示主流應用程式在適配過程中的妥協與挑戰。

摘要

極致工藝與初次上手的陌生感

作者指出，iPhone Duo作為蘋果多年來最為大膽的產品，在發售初期引發了極高的市場搶購熱潮。然而，當真正拿到手機時，除了折疊螢幕帶來的新鮮感，迎面而來的還有操作上的陌生感。其音量鍵位置偏高，機身保留了相機控制按鈕，但在喚醒與解鎖邏輯上需要重新適應。經過作者測試，需要透過特定順序的滑動與按壓組合才能達到最快解鎖，儘管這些細節有望在日後的軟體更新中逐步改善。

在展開手感方面，作者給予了極高評價。iPhone Duo擁有滑順且能單手輕鬆展開的機構設計，在完全打開時伴隨清脆的鎖定卡嗒聲，帶來療癒的感官回饋。手機內建的霧面抗眩光螢幕在降低折痕與抗反光效果上表現出色，雖然稍微犧牲了對比度與銳利度，但其紙質般的質感在閱讀長文本、瀏覽漫畫或日常多種光源環境下，皆展現出極致的高級感。

軟硬整合的設計哲學與視聽表現

作者分析，蘋果過去推廣的Liquid Glass設計語言，在 iPhone Duo 的霧面螢幕上找到了完美的歸宿。無論是視覺效果還是闔上手機時如關閉筆記本般的動畫，都體現了科技與人文的融合。針對備受關注的螢幕下前方相機，作者直言雖然仍能看出材質差異而並非完全隱形，但相較於傳統挖孔螢幕，視覺干擾已大幅降低。此外，該機在支援杜比視界（Dolby Vision）與外放揚聲器音質上的表現皆屬於業界頂尖水準。

軟體適配的現況、挑戰與未來展望

談到折疊螢幕最大的考驗——應用程式生態適配，作者認為當前許多針對相容性的批評稍顯過早，並建議消費者無須加價購買黃牛機，靜待軟體生態成熟。iPhone Duo 狹長並帶有側邊欄的特殊比例，重新分配了介面佈局，某種程度上回歸了早期 iPhone 強調的單手操作邏輯。然而，面對結構複雜、內建層層巢狀選單與促銷模組的主流大型應用，深層頁面的適配依然混亂，返回邏輯更如同捉迷藏般不一致。

作者總結，儘管大型應用的適配無法一蹴可幾，但蘋果的原生應用已立下示範標準，這同時也為獨立開發者提供了展現創意的絕佳舞台。iPhone Duo 究竟能否徹底重塑折疊螢幕市場，關鍵仍取決於開發者生態能否真正消化並活用這塊畫布。

================================================

I've watched tons of launch-day coverage. All the tech reviewers already have their units in hand and are putting them through their paces. But everyone's talking about the iPhone Duo like it reinvented the foldable form factor entirely. What exactly did Apple even change? Plenty of creators have already put out long, in-depth deep dives. So let's break this down properly: if you actually pick up the Duo, how many of your daily habits will you have to unlearn? And can this device actually reshape the entire foldable market? The iPhone Duo is Apple's most bold, aggressive product in years. and also the hardest iPhone to get your hands on at launch. Around 20 people on my team tried to snag one on pre-order day, refreshing nonstop right from the start. End result? Zero units. Not a single one. One teammate even paid scalpers a 3,000-yuan markup just to get it on release day total gut punch. Let's be real: for the Duo — and honestly every foldable phone out there novelty is the real selling point. Bigger video playback, full spreadsheet views? Those are just excuses. The real draw is how cool it looks. The second you pick it up, that fresh, new feeling hits you instantly. But right after that comes something unexpected: genuine unfamiliarity. Wait, I've tested dozens of foldables even triple-folding devices.

and I still can't wrap my head around how this one works? The volume rocker is positioned way up near the top edge. Meanwhile, the side frame keeps a dedicated camera control button but a simple tap won't wake the device or unlock it. I've worked out a few different ways to get in: tap the button then swipe up; tap and hold to trigger a long-press unlock; or swipe up first, then tap the button. That's my fastest unlock time after practicing. Not bad, right? Anyway, that's all stuff that can be fixed with software updates, no big deal. Now unfold it. The feel is totally different from any other foldable I've used. This is easily the most satisfying phone to flick open with one hand. Well I'm not just showing off for the camera, by the way. I can pop it open with barely any finger effort it unfolds so smoothly. No need to worry about your fingernails scratching the inner screen either. I've tested it thoroughly even when I swing it open ** and bump it against a table, it holds up fine. There's a latch mechanism in the hinge that clicks into place when it fully opens. That satisfying snap? Total ASMR, super therapeutic. This matte anti-glare display, when stacked up against other foldables, has noticeably better glare resistance and a far less visible crease.

That said, contrast and sharpness do take a slight hit. But when you're using it on its own, all you notice is how well it adapts to all kinds of lighting environments. Alright Quick fun fact: repeatedly folding and unfolding the screen actually does less long-term damage than leaving it folded shut all the time. The display natively has a matte finish, and that Liquid Glass design language also carries a soft matte undertone. What you see is matte, what you feel is matte it's that classic intersection of technology and the humanities, personified. The closing animation genuinely feels just like folding shut a matte paper notebook. You have to wonder: when Apple pushed Liquid Glass hard a full year ago, was it already building toward the Duo? All other Apple devices were just along for the ride, and the move totally threw every competitor off with a giant feint. That said, I've seen tons of people debating.

the under-display front camera. Let's not mince words there's no magic invisibility here. But even at its most noticeable, it's still far less intrusive than a standard punch-hole front camera. For video playback, Samsung and Huawei's foldables don't support Dolby Vision. And when it comes to speaker output, Xiaomi and Samsung models can't hold a candle to the Duo. Let's put it side by side. I think the Pura X Max is gonna have to split its "best speaker" crown with Apple now. App optimization is easily the biggest make-or-break point for any wide-form foldable. I've seen so many people nitpicking the Duo's app compatibility these past few days. But let's be realistic we're still two days "before" official customer delivery. Isn't this jumping the gun a little? From what I know, dozens of apps are already nearly fully optimized. In the next two weeks, I'm confident we'll see a massive leap in overall compatibility. So if you're considering paying scalper markup for an early unit, you might as well hold off. By the time prices drop back to retail, the app situation will be way more polished. But.

will long-term optimization ever be truly great? emmmm it's hard to say for sure. There are three key hurdles to watch: physical back navigation, the unusual aspect ratio, and the side sidebar Apple built to compensate for that ratio. Let's start with the upsides. By design, this tall, narrow form factor naturally redistributes UI elements from the top and bottom to the left and right edges. What used to sit vertically at the top shifts here, what used to sit at the bottom shifts here. Just like how the iPhone X pioneered full-screen gestures, Apple has landed on another solution that feels so obvious in hindsight. For properly optimized apps, the actual usable screen real estate doesn't shrink by much at all. In a way, this form factor actually circles back to the early iPhone ideal of true one-handed usability so much so that there's no dedicated one-handed mode anymore. When unfolded, the inner display also gives developers who don't want to phone it in a huge blank canvas to build for. That said, even a powerhouse like Apple has to meet the domestic market halfway. You can mandate optimization all you want, but China's massively popular apps built on years of tangled legacy codebases force Apple to settle for baseline, rule-based compatibility at best. Still, given Apple's mandatory requirement for developers to submit Duo-optimized app screenshots, apps with giant, unoptimized black bars should be mostly eliminated at the very least.

But most apps will likely land in that middle ground: technically optimized, but far from fully polished. To be fair, you can't write this off as developers being unmotivated or cutting corners. If anything, most teams have put in genuine effort. Look at the navigation bar in the bottom right Taobao, Alipay, iQIYI, Bilibili and Rednote have all built dedicated versions for it. By default, the bar displays no text labels; long-press it, and full labels appear. Taobao went even further, integrating labels directly into its interface, so readability and functionality made the jump almost entirely intact. But the defining trait of major domestic apps is layer upon layer of stacked features and nested menus,. plus endless promotional events and coupon giveaways. They cram every possible function into a single app, packed with webview wrappers for campaign pages, WeChat Mini Programs and even live streaming sections. The home page might be perfectly optimized, but the whole thing falls apart after just a few taps deeper. These blind spots in compatibility aren't something Apple can fix with mandates alone. We'll probably have to wait until AI takes over programming only rule-abiding AI will bother ironing out every last one of these kinks. It makes sense when you think about it. Foldables have been on the market for years. Even HarmonyOS, with its walled-off native ecosystem and full ground-up code rewrites,.

never fully ironed out these UI inconsistencies. The idea that tweaking a few lines of code will make everything work flawlessly on the iPhone Duo? There's just no way. As we all know, iPhones don't support swipe-left-to-go-back, and swipe-right-to-go-back has always been hit-or-miss. Now we've got a dedicated on-screen back button instead. Take (JD.com) for example: the back button is there, smooth as butter, and totally reachable with one hand. But tap into a subpage, and the button vanishes out of nowhere. You're forced to hunt for the back option elsewhere. Open another app, and the entire right side sits empty. the back button is dead center. Using it in practice genuinely feels like a game of whack-a-mole. Fun fact: WeChat pushed a new update the very day the Duo launched. That counts as proper optimization, right? Say I snap a random photo, jump into WeChat, and hit send. Then I change my mind how do I go back from this screen? No back button on the right, swipe-left does nothing here, same over on this side, and there's no back arrow in the top left either. It's totally frustrating.

WeChat's approach so far is to fill the main display first and leave the sidebar empty for now. They'll likely keep refining it down the line. Personally, I think the sidebar on WeChat for desktop works really well. But it's not all bad news. These giant corporate apps are probably too deeply entrenched to get a full overhaul anytime soon, but like I said earlier, this is the perfect opportunity for independent developers and smaller studios to stand out. Apple's own native iOS apps are the perfect blueprint. Calendar shows a full month view on the left and your to-do list on the right way more legible than on a candy-bar phone. Freeform, which was basically a view-only app on standard iPhones,. becomes genuinely capable when paired with a stylus. When your alarm goes off, it even has a subtle ambient lighting effect around the bezels. See? A 20,000-yuan phone really is that impressive. But then if you look at the app "Wallet" Humm Let's be honest stop roasting third-party developers for just stretching their app UIs to fit. Apple's own implementation isn't that much better. And to make this display feel genuinely distinct and satisfying, Apple even pulled off a few under-the-radar tricks, which is pretty uncharacteristic of them. I've tested dozens of wide foldables, and the camera viewfinder always has massive black bars on both sides. But on the Duo? The outer display fills the entire viewfinder with zero black bars.
